findings.claim: There is no balance sheet stress. GE Vernova doubled its dividend and increased its buyback authorisation while simultaneously funding a 50% gas turbine capacity expansion.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Reported free cash flow is exceptional and misleading in equal measure. Q2 2026 free cash flow of USD 5.1bn exceeded all of 2025, and FY2026 guidance of USD 11.5-12.5bn is roughly twice guided adjusted EBITDA of about USD 6.0bn.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE
findings.source: GE Vernova Q2 2026 results and guidance

findings.claim: Underlying free cash flow — adjusted EBITDA of roughly USD 6.0bn less capex and cash tax — is estimated at approximately USD 3.5-4.0bn, roughly a third of the reported guidance figure. The difference is customer advances on a backlog growing at 88%.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the guidance and normal capital equipment economics

findings.claim: At USD 943.34 and approximately 266m shares the market capitalisation is roughly USD 251bn. On estimated FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 6.0bn and estimated net cash of USD 10bn, the enterprise value to EBITDA multiple is approximately 40x.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: 251 market cap less 10 net cash, over 6.0 EBITDA

findings.claim: Reported price-to-earnings figures for this company are inconsistent and should not be relied on. Market data services show 26.96x and 31.44x, but Q2 net income of USD 0.6bn annualises to approximately USD 2.4bn, which against a USD 251bn market capitalisation is over 100x. Even allowing for a materially stronger second half, the multiple is well above 50x.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; reported multiples from Morningstar and analyst commentary

findings.claim: Return on invested capital cannot be assessed meaningfully. The company was separated from General Electric in April 2024, is two years into an unprecedented order cycle, and is expanding capacity 50%. There is no through-cycle record.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The genuine balance-sheet risk is the reversal of customer advances. If order intake normalises from 88% growth to flat, the working capital inflow becomes an outflow while revenue is still being recognised — a mechanism that has surprised investors in every previous capital equipment cycle.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the structure of advance-funded order books

risks.text: Reported free cash flow is roughly twice EBITDA on customer advances. The market appears to be capitalising it as if it were earnings.
When order growth normalises the working capital inflow becomes an outflow — the classic capital equipment cycle surprise.
Return on capital has no through-cycle record; the company was separated from GE in April 2024.

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 cash flow — whether the advance-driven inflow continues

conclusions: There is no balance-sheet stress: the company doubled its dividend and raised its buyback while funding a 50% capacity expansion.

But the reported free cash flow is not what it appears. FY2026 guidance of USD 11.5-12.5bn against roughly USD 6.0bn of adjusted EBITDA is free cash flow at twice earnings, which in a capital equipment business is customer advances on an order book growing 88%.

Estimated underlying free cash flow is roughly USD 3.5-4.0bn — about a third of the guided figure. On that basis the equity trades at roughly 67x cash generation rather than the 21x the headline suggests.

The honest operating multiple is approximately 40x FY2026E EBITDA. Reported price-to-earnings figures from market data services of 27-31x cannot be reconciled with Q2 net income of USD 0.6bn and should not be relied on.
Return on capital cannot be assessed: two years since separation from GE, mid-cycle, mid-expansion. There is no through-cycle record to test the bull case against.
thesisImpact: Phase 4 supplies the reason this equity is more expensive than it looks. The market is capitalising a cash flow figure that is substantially customer deposits, at a moment when order growth of 88% maximises that inflow. Phase 5 models underlying cash generation instead, and the gap between the two is the investment case.
